B's tagline, date and time are also crammed into narrow, ragged columns, and it has the same placeholder-box artifact.

In A, the quote wraps well, but the attribution breaks onto two lines and the enlarged logo is crammed right next to it, so the bottom-left corner is cluttered. The glass also sits in the top half of a fully enclosed circle, which leaves the lower half empty and loses the original's corner bleed. B keeps the original's corner-bleed circle with the glass overlapping its edge and keeps the attribution on one line, but the quote ends in an orphaned 'soon.' and the logo floats at top right with little connection to anything around it.

A keeps one clean left margin: the quote mark, headline, attribution and logo all line up, and the can and circle sit bottom-right as in the original. Its flaws are the orphaned word 'soon.' on the last headline line, a can that has shrunk to minor importance, and some empty space in the middle. B's left edges don't line up (quote mark about x55, headline about x27, attribution and logo about x50), and the headline is pushed tight to the left edge of the canvas. Its attribution touches the top of the circle and the logo sits on the circle, so the grouping looks accidental.

A: the '48H ONLY' badge has shrunk to a tiny pink dot and its text can't be read. The product box is small and pushed into the bottom-left corner, which leaves the left side looking like an afterthought. The two-column layout inside the green panel (headline beside the copy and button) is clean, but the badge is broken. B: the badge and product box stay big enough to read and keep the original's left-to-right order from badge to box to message. However, the green panel runs off the right edge of the canvas, so its margins are uneven, and the box's side face just touches the panel's left edge, which looks crowded. Still, it can be fixed and is closer to shipping than A.

I prefer A by a small margin. Its headline and subcopy are tightly grouped and stripes show on both sides of the lime panel, as in the original. But the CTA is jammed right against the end of 'price', and the '48H ONLY' badge text is tiny. B's CTA pill is oversized and competes with the headline. Its subcopy is very small, sits too low near the bottom edge, and is separated from the headline by a big gap. The lime panel runs flush to the right edge, so the layout feels lopsided.

A keeps the original three-column layout, but the CTA is now tiny and visually weaker than the enlarged LIMITED badge, so the call to action is buried. The headline also breaks awkwardly as 'The Volt / Runner', the subtitle leaves 'Thursday.' orphaned, and the CTA floats with no shared baseline. B restructures sensibly with a full-width headline and a large, prominent CTA, but the headline sits cramped against the top edge and the shoe. The headline's left edge doesn't line up with the shoe's, 'Thursday.' is still orphaned, and the LIMITED badge floats loosely off the CTA instead of sitting with the product.

A keeps a clear left-to-right order (shoe, headline, copy, badge, CTA), but the shoe is shrunk to an icon, the headline breaks awkwardly onto two lines as 'The Volt / Runner', the 3-line body copy is very small, and the LIMITED pill is nearly as big as Enter Now, so the two compete. B's single-line headline is strong, but the shoe is a speck squeezed into the top-right with the LIMITED badge jammed against it and the top edge. The button is stacked tightly under them, so the right cluster is cramped, the product comes after the copy, and the body text is even tinier.

A reworks the layout for the new shape: confetti and the book sit in a left panel and the card is on the right, so the strong headline stands out and the brand feel survives. Its flaws: the Inkwell & Lantern logo is tiny and jammed into the card's top-left corner, out of line with the right-aligned eyebrow; the card runs to the top and right canvas edges with no margin; and the fine print beside the CTA is nearly body size and competes with the button. B is just the original shrunk and stacked: the confetti is reduced to a thin strip at the top, the book, logo, eyebrow, headline, body, CTA and fine print are crammed into a tight column with almost no gaps, the logo can't be read, and the fine print is tiny.

A is clean and has no collisions, but the headline is too small for a 768-wide banner. The '7 days free' fine print is so tiny it can't be read, and a large dead gap separates the text block from the CTA, which is stranded at the far right. B gets the hierarchy right with a big headline, but it is badly cramped: the headline sits against the top edge, the fine print against the bottom, and the phone is clipped at the right edge and touches the top and bottom. The CTA also floats off-centre and doesn't line up with the left-aligned headline or fine print.

A reads cleanly in the original order: headline, then a small phone, then the CTA pill, then the fine print. Its flaws are a phone so tiny the 7.2 gauge is unreadable, and fine print wrapped onto three cramped lines at nearly headline weight against the right edge. B puts the phone after the legal copy, so it reads as an afterthought jammed against the right edge, almost touching the three-line fine print. That cluster is cramped and the product is reduced to a speck, which weakens both hierarchy and fidelity.
